marais: The Marais and Place des Vosges
Rue des Rosiers and the narrow streets of the Marais, then Place des Vosges, the oldest square in Paris (1612), with its arcades and a garden in the middle.
notredame: Notre-Dame and Île de la Cité

The cathedral reopened in December 2024 after the fire. Entry is free: book a free time slot on the official site notredamedeparis.fr (slots open 48 hours ahead, at midnight) to skip the queue, which can take over an hour without a booking. Then a walk around Île de la Cité and along the Seine.
saintechapelle: The most spectacular Gothic stained glass in Paris, 5 minutes from Notre-Dame. Booking a time slot is required: do it online before you leave.
louvre: The Pyramid and the Cour Napoléon, then the Palais-Royal courtyard with Buren's columns and the Jardin des Tuileries. From the outside it's all free.
eiffel: Get off at Trocadéro for the classic view from the esplanade, cross the Pont d'Iéna, walk under the tower and carry on along the Champ de Mars to École Militaire.
arc: The arch up close (reach it through the underpass, not by crossing the roundabout) and a stretch of the Champs-Élysées.
montmartre: From Abbesses: the Wall of Love, the lanes of Rue des Trois Frères, the steps (or the funicular) up to Sacré-Cœur, then Place du Tertre and La Maison Rose.
louvremus: Inside the museum: the Mona Lisa, the Venus de Milo, the Winged Victory of Samothrace and the Napoleon III apartments. Pick two or three wings: you couldn't see it all in a week.
orsay: The Impressionists in an old railway station: Monet, Renoir, Van Gogh, Degas. On the fifth floor, the view of Paris through the great clock.
stgermain: The oldest church in Paris, the streets of bookshops and galleries between Rue de Buci and Rue de Seine, then Saint-Sulpice.
latin: The Sorbonne, the Panthéon and Rue Mouffetard, then the Jardin du Luxembourg with the Medici Fountain and the Senate palace.
opera: The grand staircase and gilded foyer of the Opéra Garnier, then the free rooftop terrace of the Galeries Lafayette, with views of the Opéra and the Eiffel Tower.
canal: The iron footbridges, the locks and the cafés of the Parisians' favourite neighbourhood, from République towards Jaurès.
perelachaise: The world's most famous park cemetery: the graves of Jim Morrison, Oscar Wilde, Édith Piaf and Chopin along tree-lined avenues.
versailles: The King's and Queen's apartments and the Hall of Mirrors. Arrive at opening time: from 11am the rooms fill up.
trianon: The French formal gardens, the Grand Canal and Marie Antoinette's estate: the Petit Trianon and the Queen's Hamlet.
